approach: Add one reading check, `check_records_measure`, in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs`, next to `check_history_fixture`. It uses the same gate (`changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`, surveys.rs:237). It looks for a records-computed measure in the summary and every criterion, matched as whole words on lowercase text with `has_phrase`: throughput, keep rule, planning cost, refusal rate(s), check duration(s), landing time(s). Hyphens and underscores count as spaces, and the sentence "higher refusal rate is intended" is removed first. That sentence is the one the reader brief tells readers to write for every refusal rule (reader.rs:311), and without the removal the check would refuse those readings. The reading is accepted only when one Behavior criterion names `real records`, an independent source (`git log`, `recorded check durations` or `recorded durations`) and an `expected range`. Otherwise the check refuses, naming the matched measure and each missing part. The check goes in as one `step!(check_records_measure(reading));` line in `refusing_check` (`crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:538`), directly after `check_history_fixture`, so the existing order tests still hold. That file is not in the brief's deliverable list but is where the chain lives. The step line forces a refusing case in `crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs` (`every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case`, line 2733); that file is also unlisted. Unit tests go in the `reading.rs` test module, reusing `code_reading`, `add_behavior`, `accept` and `gate_refuser`. The reader and planner rule lines go where the brief text is built: `READING_RULES` in `briefs/reader.rs:287` (11 to 12 entries, at most 220 characters) and a new const `REAL_RECORDS_RULE` in `briefs/planner.rs`, added to the Report format string at planner.rs:134. The `briefs.rs` tests are updated: rule count 12, section limit raised from 3150, a planner-line test. CHANGELOG gets one item. The reader and planner token budgets (`BudgetSet`) cover only the prompt files and are not touched, because the brief lines sit outside them (docs/system-facts.md "Prompt sets and budgets"; `computed_rows` in `crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs:21-80` composes only `CONTRACT`, the frames, `defaults` and `catalog`). The "2 and 95 tokens left" assumption in the reading therefore does not constrain these lines. The size limits that do bind are the 220-character line limit and the section limit at briefs.rs:3501 and 3558.

decisions.choice: Match records-computed measures by a phrase list over the summary and every criterion, and do not match deliverable paths.
decisions.reason: The gate and helpers (`has_phrase`, `straight_lowercase`) already exist and cost no model call. Path triggers would flag every edit to a file such as `status.rs` (61 keyword hits), which holds many unrelated things. The request names the measures in words.

rejected.option: Also trigger on deliverable paths such as `status/throughput.rs`.
rejected.why: It flags refactors that change no figure. It is also a second matching rule needing its own corpus cases.

rejected.option: Ask a model to judge whether the change touches a records measure.
rejected.why: It adds a model call and is not reproducible; the property is visible in the reading text.

decisions.choice: Remove the sentence 'higher refusal rate is intended' before scanning, and match 'refusal rate' otherwise.
decisions.reason: The reader brief (briefs/reader.rs:311) tells readers to write that sentence for every refusal rule, so a naive 'refusal rate' trigger would refuse the readings that comply with the other rule. No existing test reading mixes the keyword with a code reading, which I checked by grep.

rejected.why: The request names refusal rates as a measure.
It misses the singular; stripping the one known phrase is narrower.

decisions.choice: Satisfy the rule only with one Behavior criterion that holds all three parts: `real records`, an independent source (`git log` / `recorded check durations`) and `expected range`. A Content criterion does not count.
decisions.reason: The failures in the request came from criteria checked on fixtures, which the verifier can run. A part spread across criteria could leave the real-records criterion with no range, which is how a wrong figure passes. The refusal text names each missing part and gives an example criterion.

rejected.option: Accept the parts spread across several criteria.
rejected.why: No single criterion then ties the real run to the independent range.

rejected.option: Require the range to be numeric.
rejected.why: Numeric detection is a new parser with its own corpus forms, and the lexical phrase `expected range` matches the existing style of `check_history_fixture`.

decisions.choice: The refusal text says that a criterion which reads `git log` also needs an `Environment:` assumption (`check_environment_reach`).
decisions.reason: `git log` is in ENV_LOCATED_SOURCES (surveys.rs:561-567), and a read verb such as `from` within 6 words triggers C1 (surveys.rs:840-841). A reader who follows the new hint would be refused again by the later check, and the reader gets only one second read (reader.rs:340-342).

rejected.option: Say nothing and let `check_environment_reach` refuse next.
rejected.why: It burns the one second read on a predictable second refusal.

decisions.choice: Put the brief lines in `briefs/reader.rs` and `briefs/planner.rs`, and the tests in `briefs.rs`.
decisions.reason: `briefs.rs` only declares `mod planner; mod reader;` (briefs.rs:17-18) and holds the tests. `READING_RULES` (reader.rs:287) and the planner Report text (planner.rs:134) are where the text is built.

rejected.why: They would not reach the briefs, so the brief tests would not see them.

risks.risk: Acceptance criterion 1 says the added lines are in `briefs.rs`, but the text is built in `briefs/reader.rs` and `briefs/planner.rs`; `briefs.rs` holds only the tests (briefs.rs:17-18, 3493). The planner const also adds a format interpolation, and the `briefs.rs` tests add several lines.
risks.mitigation: The demonstration for criterion 1 greps the diff of the two sub-module files, where there is one rule line each. The plan lists all three files so the verifier does not expect the lines in `briefs.rs` alone.

risks.risk: False positives: ordinary readings that mention a measure word (for example a docs-adjacent code change that only displays throughput) are refused.
risks.mitigation: The gate requires a capability, no question, class code or tests, and a Behavior criterion. The carve-out removes 'higher refusal rate is intended'. The refusal text says exactly what to add. Few past jobs touch these measures, so 3% is declared (an estimate, not measured). The replay at verification measures the real share, and a share above the declared one plus 5 points holds the job.

risks.risk: The check is lexical. A criterion can contain the three phrases without running anything on real records, or a measure can be named in unlisted words ('merge latency').
risks.mitigation: The limits are stated in the doc comment, as for `check_history_fixture`. The check ensures the criterion exists; the verifier runs it against the evidence snapshot, which `briefs.rs` `evidence_section` already provides. Making the verifier fetch records is out of scope.

risks.risk: A reader who satisfies the rule with `git log` is then refused by `check_environment_reach` and has only one second read.
risks.mitigation: The refusal text tells the reader to add an `Environment:` assumption when the criterion reads git history. The accepted tests include one, so the chain is tested end to end.

risks.risk: The reader section limit (briefs.rs:3558, below 3150 bytes) is near its limit. One more line of at most 220 characters can pass it.
risks.mitigation: The test limit is raised to the measured new size plus a small margin, with the comment updated as the earlier entries do. The 220-character line limit stays.
